Commentary.Commentary: South Africa will be more than pleased with this. Not only have they got a healthy lead, but they must have surely worn out the Pakistan players a little more. With the wicket misbehaving as it has been, the hosts will be raring to have a go with the ball. The action will begin shortly. Don't go anywhere.

So the Proteas have been dismissed rather early, but not before they got some quick and vital runs from the tail. De Kock and Philander, the overnight batsmen, the more recognized ones, were sent back by Amir rather quickly. He got Rabada early too and it seemed like they could contain them for quite less, but Steyn and Olivier found the fence on several occasions which took the lead past 250.

OUT! That should do it. Pakistan have got the final wicket. Short ball from around the wicket, on middle and off, Steyn backs away to slap it over covers. Gets a top edge to the same area where Fakhar Zaman takes a simple catch. SOUTH AFRICA HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 431!
Full ball on middle and leg, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single. 12 runs off this one, an entertaining over comes to an end.

That's got to hurt. Seeing Steyn give the charge, Amir pounds it in short outside leg. It catches the batsman on the helmet as he tries to take the pull shot on. No harm done though, he seems to be alright.
No ball! Third's time a charm. Amir oversteps for the third straight occasion and this time the umpire spots it. Back of a length around off, Steyn fails to make connection.

SIX! That's outta here! Wonderful stuff, Dale Steyn. The off cutter on the stumps, fuller in length, the batsman stays leg side and slogs it over mid-wicket for a maximum. Amir has overstepped again, the umpire has missed it once more.
A little short, Steyn once again swings across the line but makes no connection. Amir overstepped by a huge margin there, but the umpire didn't spot it.
Good length ball rising off the surface, Steyn swings hard but fails to connect.
FOUR! Now Dale Steyn joins in on the fun. Doesn't want to be left out. It's full and in his arc, he clears his front leg, picks his spot and lofts it over mid on for a boundary.

FOUR! 11 off the over, expensive one from Afridi. All these are bonus runs for South Africa. Back of a length outside off, Olivier plays at it and it goes off the edge. Flies well past gully and away to the third man fence.
Around off, defended from within the crease.
Back of a length outside off, it goes off the outer half and past gully. The fielder chases it down and keeps the batsmen down to two.
FOUR! That is a terrific shot. It's banged in short and Olivier takes the pull shot on. Connects perfectly as he hits it over square leg for a boundary.
Back of a length close to off, kept out safely.
Starts from around the wicket, a length ball angling in on off, Steyn plays it from the outer half square on the off side for a run.
Shaheen Afridi brought into the attack.
Drags his length back by a fraction, keeps it around off, the batsman pushes it to the covers.
A little bit of movement away, fuller and around off, Olivier plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Full inswinging delivery on off, Olivier brings down a straight blade in defense.
Duanne Olivier to bat next.

OUT! Rolling back the years are you, Amir? That's an absolute ripper. What a sight to behold. Superb delivery. Pitches it full on middle and it swings away ever so much, Rabada plays down the wrong line and that's his undoing. All three stumps are shattered. Amazing.
Full delivery on off, Steyn drives it on the up to mid off and takes a single.
Dale Steyn is the next batsman in.

OUT! Bowled 'em! That's the second one down for the morning. Beautiful delivery from Mohammad Amir. Bowls a length ball on off and makes it come back in late. Philander plays away from his body, gets an inside edge and drags it back onto the stumps. Pakistan celebrate. South Africa lead by 230 runs.
Short of a length outside off, punched off the back foot through covers for a brace.
Good length ball around off, kept out from the back foot.

FOUR! Not what he intended to do, but gets runs for it. Rabada has a little laugh at it too. Full delivery angling in on off, Rabada looks to push down the ground but it goes off the inner half and past mid-wicket. Afridi gives it the chase but can't keep it inside the rope.
A little ahead of a length, close to off, Kagiso is forward in defense.
FOUR! Spills it on the pads and pays the price. Abbas bowls it full and Rabada flicks it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Lands it on a length on middle and leg, flicked into the leg side for nothing.
Angling across Philander, outside off, he lets it be.
Outside off, it goes off the outer half past gully for one.
Beaten! A length ball in the off stump channel, moving away slightly and late, Rabada looks to defend but the ball goes past the outside edge.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Too straight in line, worked away on the leg side.
Sharp bounce. On a back of a length, on off, Philander is taken by surprise as the ball takes the glove and hits him on the thigh pad.
Back of a length on off, Rabada looks to play at it and gets an inside edge which hits his boot and rolls beside the off stump.
Length ball cutting back in on middle, played off the inner half in front of mid-wicket.
Angling away from outside off, steered to point with an angled bat to point.
Sharp bumper, close to off, takes Rabada by surprise as he barely manages to sway away from the line.
On the shorter side of things, into the body, Vernon with a little swivel pulls it down to fine leg for a single.
Short ball banged in, ducked and evaded by the batsman.
Kagiso Rabada walks out to bat.

OUT! Edged and gone! Pakistan will enjoy this. Amir strikes in his very first over. Just behind a length, outside off, de Kock just loosely plays at this. Gets a thick edge and it flies to Asad Shafiq at second slip. He dives to his left and takes a good catch. The dangerous de Kock is dismissed, this is the best start possible for the visitors.
FOUR! Poor line and it's duly punished. Full and on the pads, de Kock flicks it neatly past the diving mid-wicket fielder and finds the fence. Too easy for a player of his quality.
Coming in at first but then shaping away late, on a length around off. Quinton de Kock is watchful as he presents the full face of the bat.
Hurled too far outside off, the southpaw raises his bat and lets it through.
Touch straight in line, worked square on the leg side but for no run.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, de Kock has nothing to do with it.
Mohammad Amir to bowl from the other end.
FOUR! Two in a row, fine way to end the over. Back of a length, rising off the deck outside off, Philander stands tall, opens the bat face and punches it through cover-point to find the fence.
FOUR! First runs of the morning and what a beautiful shot from Vernon Philander. Full and outside off, he just leans into the drive and caresses it through the covers for a boundary.
Full delivery angling in on middle and leg, driven back down the ground towards mid on.
The pitch already misbehaving. The last one didn't bounce and this took off. Shaping back in from around off, on a length, Vernon leaves it alone.
Not much bounce on this occasion, outside off, left alone this time.
Good length delivery just around off, Philander comes half forward and defends it down on the off side.
We are ready to get underway. Quinton de Kock walks out to the middle with Vernon Philander. Mohammad Abbas will start proceedings off with the ball. Two slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

Welcome for the third, and what could cynically be considered, as the last day of this Newlands Test. South Africa already have a lead of 205 runs, that is largely down to the heroics of captain Faf and Bavuma. De Kock then piled the pressure on and is unbeaten on 55 with Philander to partner him. Pakistan have looked toothless with the ball, and Abbas seemingly still struggling with injury hasn't aided their cause either. Will their batting come to the party finally? Because that's the only thing that can save them. We'll find out soon enough what unfolds.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

The ball firmly in South Africa's court as things stand. They will try to add another 50-60 runs at least and then have a go at the away side with the ball. Pakistan, well, will try to wrap up the remaining Protea wickets ASAP. The action from Day 3 will begin at 1030 local (0830 GMT). Do join in for that. Cheers!

Afridi eventually dismissed both Bavuma and du Plessis, which did give them something to smile about, but de Kock didn't let that last long. He motored himself along to a fluent fifty and extended the lead to 205. Pakistan bowled well for the most part, just that luck wasn't on their side. Also a few dropped chances did not aid their cause. It was a long day for the visitors on the field.

South Africa's day without a doubt. They have taken this Test match into their stride and it's all thanks to the fine work from du Plessis and Bavuma. After Abbas and Afridi took out Amla and de Bruyn in the first hour, the Faf-Temba pair completely stole the show. It added 156 runs, with Bavuma scoring a fine 75 and the skipper notching up a skillful ton.
Quicker and flatter on middle, de Kock works it towards mid-wicket. AND THAT IS STUMPS ON DAY 2. SOUTH AFRICA ARE 382/6. AND LEAD BY 205 RUNS.
Slower through the air on middle, de Kock defends it with a straight bat.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

NOT OUT! Quinton de Kock survives. Yasir flights it up on middle, de Kock tries to defend it off the front foot. The ball spins back sharply, hitting the pads and it lobs up in the air. Sarfraz comes forward and collects it. Sarfraz straightaway goes for the review. He is confident that it has hit his bat. The replay shows no ultraedge and the de Kock survives. Waste of a review and they lose both of them as well.
Quinton de Kock is the man in question here for an lbw decision.
Drags it short on middle, Quinton defends it off the front foot and onto the ground.
A touch short on middle, de Kock defends it from within the crease.
Fuller on middle, VP flicks it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full on his pads, Philander nudges it to the leg side.
Quicker on off, Vernon drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Full on off, de Kock strokes it towards long off for a single.
Flatter on middle, de Kock defends it with a straight bat.
Quicker through the air on off, met with a straight blade in defense.
Spinning away from outside off, fuller in length, Philander opens the bat face and runs it past short third man. Collects a brace for doing so.
Vernon plants his front foot forward and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Loopy leg break, easily dealt with by the batsman.
Slower through the air and full on the stumps, Philander once again is forward in defense.
Tossed up on off, Philander comes forward and defends.

Fuller on middle and leg, de Kock flicks it through square leg for a couple of runs.
Fuller on middle, Quinton defends it with a straight bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Drags it short on middle, the batsman punches it towards point.

FOUR! Deft touch. A touch short on middle, de Kock opens the face of the bat and guides it through third man for a boundary. Brings up his 14th Test fifty. He has completely dominated the Pakistan attack.
Asad Shafiq to roll his arm over.
Strays on his pads, the batsman tucks it around the corner for a run.
Fuller again on off, de Kock drives it through covers for a brace.
A tad fuller on off, Philander drives it through covers for a single.
Fuller on middle, Vernon drives it towards covers.
Quicker on middle, the batsman nudges it around the corner for a run.

Nicely played! Philander squirts it away behind square on the off side and takes two. Lead into the 190s now.
Fuller in length around off, de Kock strokes it towards wide mid off for a single.
On the fuller side, de Kock looks to drive but it goes off the inner half towards mid on.
Back of a length around off, de Kock guides it through point for a couple.
FOUR! Easy-peasy! Full and on the pads, de Kock is too good a batsman to miss out on that. He flicks it through mid-wicket and the ball races away to the fence.
The googly by Yasir, Philander defends it off the front foot.
Watchfully turns it around the corner for another single.
On the stumps, de Kock easily clips it to mid-wicket.
Nicely tossed up on off, Philander eases it to long off for a run.
Slightly shorter this time, de Kock goes back and nudges it towards fine leg for a single.
Tosses it up on off, de Kock works it towards mid-wicket with the turn.
Vernon Philander is the new man in.

OUT! Finally a wicket for Pakistan. Faf du Plessis departs. What an innings from the captain. He was under pressure coming into this Test after getting ducks in both the innings of the first Test. Coming to the delivery, it is a length delivery on off, Faf du Plessis tries to defend it, but gets a faint edge on it and straight to the keeper. Sarfraz thinks about it and goes for the review. The replay shows there is some spike on the bat and Faf has to make the long walk back to the pavilion. He has grinded out as it was tough to play in the morning session. Standing ovation for the captain for his outstanding knock. He deserves it. He has made sure that South Africa are in a commanding position after the end of day's play.
Du Plessis is the man in question here for caught behind.

Quicker and flatter on middle, de Kock punches it towards point.

Starts off with a wide delivery outside off, de Kock tries to cut it but misses it completely.
Shaheen Afridi is back on. They are trying everything to get a wicket here.
A single to end as de Kock plays the conventional sweep to the man at deep backward square leg. A single taken.
Well bowled! Tosses it up outside off, de Kock goes back to a delivery which he should have played forward to. He tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
FOUR! The reverse sweep is out and it has been hit really well. 2000 Test match runs for de Kock. He hits it fine on the off side and the ball races away.
Flatter and outside off, Faf guides it through point for a single.
This is tossed up around off, de Kock strokes it down to long off for a single.
FOUR! Welcome back into the attack! Short and wide outside off, de Kock waits for it and then guides it through point for a boundary. Runs coming thick and fast now.
Yasir Shah is back on.
On the off pole, Faf lunges and keeps it out.
Angles this into the off pole, Faf du Plessis is solid in defense.
Back of a length on off, it is kept out.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Works it with the angle to the man at mid-wicket.

Cut him into half! Length ball outside off, it comes back in. De Kock tries to defend but is beaten by the inward movement. The ball beats the inside edge and goes to the keeper. Abbas stands there with a frustrated look, he has beaten the inside edge, the outside edge, but luck has just not been on his side.
Once again Faf du Plessis is early into the pull shot. It goes off the toe end towards mid off.
Faf is receiving some medical attention. He looks fine, but you never want to take chances with head injuries.
RIGHT ON THE BADGE! A bumper by Amir, Faf is a little too early into the pull. He misses and the ball hits him on the helmet.
Down the leg side, de Kock fails to flick it. Sarfraz behind does not collect it cleanly and concedes a bye. Has not been at his best has Sarfraz in the last few overs. A little sloppy.
Full and on the pads, it is clipped through mid-wicket and the batsmen take two.
A huge appeal but not given! On a length and around off, it comes back in after pitching. De Kock tries to defend but the ball hits him high on the pad.

100 for Faf du Plessis, his 9th in Test cricket and what an innings this has been. He came out when they had lost two quick wickets and he has shown excellent character here on a wicket which is very difficult to bat on. Copped a few blows but continued to craft a brilliant innings. He gets to the milestone with another excellently timed shot. It is slightly full and around off, he strokes it through covers. It does not have enough legs to get to the boundary but the batsmen run three. He pumps his fist as he completes the third. Takes his helmet off and soaks in all the applause by the crowd. Well deserved. Well played skipper, you have led from the front here.
Back of a length on off, de Kock was trying to cut it but misses it completely.
Fuller on off, Quinton pushes it towards point.
Length delivery on middle, de Kock defends it off the front foot.
Length delivery on middle, du Plessis taps it towards point for a run.

DROPPED! Huge moment in the game. Fuller on leg, du Plessis flicks it and Sarfraz goes to his left and he gets both his hands to it and still drops it. Lazy effort from Sarfraz behind the stumps. He should have caught it. That was a sitter. Sarfraz normally takes brilliant catches but he will be disappointed with that effort. Abbas is frustrated as well. Luck is not going their way today, with some play and misses and edges not carrying. That wicket would have changed the momentum. Is that the turning point of the game? We have to wait and watch.
Length delivery on middle and leg, Faf works it to mid-wicket.

Back of a length on middle, de Kock works it towards square leg.
On the pads, Faf hops and then works it through square leg. A run is taken.
Goes wide of the crease and bowls it on off, Faf defends it off the front foot.
A bumper on middle, Faf du Plessis ducks under it at the very last.

Back of a length around off, de Kock stands tall and guides it to point.
On a length and outside off, de Kock shoulders arms to it.
Once again it is on the pads, de Kock clips it through mid-wicket and takes another brace. The first two balls is where Abbas should be bowling, this is a little too straight.
A little too straight this time, de Kock flicks it through square leg for a couple.
BEATEN! On a length and once again it angles away. De Kock plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Well bowled! Lands it around off, it pitches and moves away. De Kock tries to defend but gets an outside edge towards covers.
Drinks!
A touch short on off, the batsman punches it towards point.
NO BALL! Amir oversteps. It was bowled a touch short on middle, Faf pulls it through square leg. Surprisingly, they did not take a run.
Goes short this time on middle, Faf nicely ducks underneath it.
Fuller on off, du Plessis drives it straight to the mid off fielder.
Back of a length outside off, du Plessis does not need to play at those.
Length delivery this time on off, Faf defends it from within the crease.

Cutting back in from a good length, takes the inside edge of Quinton's bat and thuds onto the pads as he tries to play at it.
Outside off on a good length, left alone.

The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Landing on middle and it shapes back in, catches de Kock on the front pad and a loud appeal goes up. Height is always the issue.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drifts on his pads, the batsman works it towards fine leg for a run.
Length delivery on middle, de Kock defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Luck is not going with Amir's way. Back of a length delivery on middle, de Kock was trying to defend it but the ball kept rising and hits him high on the bat. The ball then flies off the bat and through slip cordon for a boundary.
That was close. Back of a length on middle, de kock defends it but the ball bounces back and goes just over the stumps. Lucky escape for de Kock. De Kock will be relieved it did not hit the stumps.
Fuller on middle and leg, de Kock flicks it straight to the square leg fielder.

Full on middle and leg, de Kock works it to the leg side for a run.
Good length delivery on off,  de Kock tries to defend it, but the ball bounces after pitching and hitting the gloves of the batsman in the process.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single. End of an action packed over, 13 runs but an important wicket from it.

So easily could have been three in a row! Full and on off, asking to be hit. De Kock drives it firmly but straight to the man at covers. A little to the left or the right and it would have been three in a row.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for de Kock to begin with. This is short and outside off, de Kock waits for it and then guides it through short third man for another boundary.
FOUR! A gift for de Kock on the first ball. A full toss on the pads, de Kock says thank you very much as he flicks it through backward square leg for a boundary.
Quinton de Kock is the new man in for South Africa.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Shaheen Afridi provides the breakthrough Pakistan so desperately wanted. Ends the 150-plus run stand, ends a magnificent knock by Bavuma on a very, very difficult wicket. He walks off to a standing ovation and he deserves every bit of it. Coming to the ball now, it is on a length and around off, it is angled into the batter first, Bavuma tries to play the original trajectory but it pitches and then moves away. Takes the outside edge and Sarfraz takes a good catch diving to his right. Can this now open the floodgates? Pakistan will hope so.
FOUR! That went to the fence like a tracer bullet. It is short and on the body, Bavuma helps it on its way to the fine leg fence. No stopping those.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

This partnership is taking the game away from Pakistan. The visitors need quick wickets otherwise they will be staring down the barrel. South Africa will like these two to continue for a longer period of time.

Fuller on off, Bavuma pushes it towards covers. Bavuma takes off, du Plessis still goes for the run. The fielder at point collect and has a shy at the strikers end but misses it. He would have been a goner had he hit the stumps. Faf du plessis was miles out of the crease.

They can't believe it has not gone in their favour. The look on their faces says it all. They were in desperate need of this wicket, they felt they had got it only for the DRS to overturn the decision.

Brilliant session for South Africa. They have scored at around three runs per over and have gone wicketless. The captain, Faf du Plessis and Temba Bavuma are amidst a 132-run stand and are taking the game away from the visitors. They have dominated the bowlers and would look to do the same in the last session. For the visitors, they have not been at their best, leaking easy runs. However, with the new ball being taken, Sarfraz will be hoping for the fast bowlers to take some wickets and wrap the innings up as soon as possible. Could be a defining session for both the teams.

They need a few wickets quickly after Lunch and get into the South African lower order. Will they be able to do so or will the home team continue to stay ahead? Join us to find out in a while.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the second Test between South Africa and Pakistan. The hosts are in a commanding position at the moment and they will look to have a stronger hold on the game by the end of today. A big lead is what they will be looking for on a wicket which seems to have eased off. Pakistan on the other hand, need a few quick wickets if they are to get back in the game. They need one of their bowlers to step up and deliver the goods. Will someone do so? Also, we saw the bowlers dominate yesterday, will we see the same today? Stay tuned to find out in a while.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Now then, what will we have in store for us on Day 2? Will the hosts continue the domination or will Pakistan fight back? Join us to find out at 1030 local (0830 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Credit though has to be given to the Protea bowlers. Earlier in the day, they made quick work of the Pakistan batting line-up and bundled them out for a pretty low score with all the bowlers taking a wicket at least. Olivier was the star once again as he finished with a four-fer. For Pakistan, had it not been for their skipper who scored a half ton, even getting to 100 would have been difficult. In reply, The South African batters have started off really well and they would now look to continue the same.

A wicket right at the end gives Pakistan something to smile about. However, it has been all South Africa today. They head into Day 2 in a very commanding position, courtesy some outstanding batting by their top order in the final session. First it was Markram and Elgar who added a 56-run stand, then the former, along with Amla, stitched another 50-plus stand. The opener was dismissed in an unfortunate manner after playing a fluent innings. One though would feel he has done a good enough job for his side. The hosts trail by only 54 more runs and have a lot of batting to come.

OUT! TIMBER! Wicket off the last ball of the day. And it comes from the most unlikely source - Shan Masood. What a masterstroke from Sarfraz Ahmed. Delight for Pakistan. However, this is a very fortunate dismissal for them. Nothing Markram could have done about that. It is a touch short on off, it pitches and jags back. Keeps very low. It almost seemed like it never left the ground. Markram tries to defend it from the crease but then seeing the bad bounce, tries to adjust, is not able to do so and the ball knocks the off stump out. Markram can't believe it as he trudges off in disgust. He was looking all set for a big one but luck was not on his side. THAT WILL ALSO BE STUMPS ON DAY 1. SOUTH AFRICA ARE 123/2.
